title: kith-tslocal: WhoIs response types
description:
Define Rust structs for WhoIs response that map to Tailscale LocalAPI /localapi/v0/whois JSON.

What: Define UserProfile, Node, WhoIsResponse in kith-tslocal/src/lib.rs (or dedicated module).

Tailscale JSON field names (from real tailscale source):
- WhoIsResponse.UserProfile: { ID, LoginName, DisplayName, ProfilePicURL }
- WhoIsResponse.Node: { Name, Addresses: [netip.Prefix], ... }

Algorithm:
1. Define struct UserProfile with serde rename_all=PascalCase (or explicit rename per field):
   - id: String  (maps to JSON 'ID')
   - login_name: String  (maps to JSON 'LoginName')
   - display_name: Option<String>  (maps to JSON 'DisplayName')
   - profile_pic_url: Option<String>  (maps to JSON 'ProfilePicURL', not needed for auth but parse to avoid unknown field errors)
2. Define struct Node with minimal fields needed:
   - name: String  (maps to JSON 'Name')
   - addresses: Vec<String>  (maps to JSON 'Addresses', netip.Prefix as string)
   Use #[serde(default)] on fields that may be absent.
3. Define struct WhoIsResponse:
   - node: Node  (maps to JSON 'Node')
   - user_profile: UserProfile  (maps to JSON 'UserProfile')
   Use #[serde(rename_all = 'PascalCase')] at struct level.
4. All structs derive: Debug, Clone, Deserialize (no Serialize needed - not sent on wire)
5. Validate invariants: user_profile.id must not be empty; checked at use site, not in type
6. Run: cargo test -p kith-tslocal; cargo clippy -p kith-tslocal -- -D warnings

Defensive rules:
- UserProfile.id is OPAQUE - do not add parsing methods or format assumptions
- Use #[serde(default)] on optional Node fields that tailscale may add/remove across versions
- Do NOT use #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] - tailscale adds new fields in minor versions

Agent team: standard (R + I + T)
Tests: unit-level deserialization tests using hardcoded JSON strings matching the spec.
- Test: valid full WhoIsResponse JSON parses correctly (field mapping correct)  
- Test: missing DisplayName field -> None (not an error)
- Test: extra JSON fields are ignored (forward compat)
Oracle: the JSON fixtures are hand-constructed from Tailscale LocalAPI spec.
